territorial_scope.description: Addressed to named DoD organizations and governs DoD design, testing, fielding and employment of weapon systems; the text states no geographic limit.

summary.short: DoD Directive 3000.09 sets DoD policy for the design, testing, approval, fielding and employment of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems. It requires senior review and approval of certain autonomous weapon systems before formal development and again before fielding, and sets verification and testing requirements. Effective January 25, 2023.
summary.long: DoD Directive 3000.09, effective January 25, 2023, applies to DoD organizations and to the design, development, acquisition, testing, fielding and employment of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems. It excludes cyberspace capabilities, unarmed platforms, unguided and manually guided munitions, mines, unexploded ordnance and non-weapon systems. It requires that systems allow commanders and operators to exercise appropriate levels of human judgment over the use of force, and sets verification, validation and test-and-evaluation requirements, including for AI capabilities. Certain autonomous weapon systems require senior review and approval by named DoD officials before formal development and again before fielding. Certain semi-autonomous, defensive and non-lethal systems are exempt from that review. International sales or transfers follow existing technology security processes. The directive assigns responsibilities to the Under Secretaries, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, DOT&E, the CDAO, the CJCS, the Military Departments and Combatant Commanders, and establishes an Autonomous Weapon System Working Group. A Deputy Secretary of Defense waiver is available for urgent military need. The excerpt sets out no penalty provisions. It reissues and cancels the November 21, 2012 directive of the same title.

notes: Plaintext omits introductory material, the chart and references, so any legal basis or further amending or implementing act is not visible here; relation status is not_found. Cross-referenced DoD issuances are cited by number only; target_instrument_id is null because none is in the registry. The text names the strategy inconsistently as 'Responsible AI Strategy' (e.g., 1.2.f) and 'Responsible Artificial Intelligence Strategy' (e.g., 2.12.b). Sec. 1.2.c and Sec. 4.1 set senior review requirements that are repeated across sections.

events.date_text: Approved by: Kathleen H. Hicks, Deputy Secretary of Defense

thresholds.note: The directive contains no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Scope and approval triggers are qualitative (e.g., 'substantially differ' in Para 1.2.c(2) and 4.1.a), and 'formal development' is tied to a milestone reference (Glossary G.2) rather than a number. Dates, paragraph numbers and the 'urgent military need' waiver (Para 4.2) carry no numeric threshold.
